original_question: Is the additivity number add(S_1(Γ, Γ)) equal to b?
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the exact open problem in the paper almost verbatim. It correctly targets the open-cover property S1(Γ, Γ) from Section 8.3, Problem 11, and correctly asks whether its additivity number is the bounding number b, rather than drifting to the neighboring problems add(Ufin(Γ, O)) or add(S1(O, O)).
missing_details: The ambient objects are sets of reals; this is the paper's default scope unless otherwise stated.
Γ denotes the family of open γ-covers of a space X, not the Borel family BΓ.
A cover is taken to be nontrivial: X = ⋃U and X is not itself a member of U.
A γ-cover is an infinite open cover such that each x in X belongs to all but finitely many members of the cover.
S1(Γ, Γ) means: for every sequence ⟨U_n : n in ω⟩ of members of Γ(X), one can choose U_n in U_n for each n so that {U_n : n in ω} is again a γ-cover of X.
To be stand-alone, add(S1(Γ, Γ)) should be spelled out as the least cardinal κ such that there exists a family {X_α : α < κ} of sets of reals, each satisfying S1(Γ, Γ), whose union fails S1(Γ, Γ).
b should be defined as the bounding number: the least size of an unbounded family in ω^ω under eventual domination ≤*.
If one wants full fidelity to the paper's conventions, one may note that for sets of reals the relevant covers may be assumed countable.
The nearby context in the paper also records the known bounds h ≤ add(S1(Γ, Γ)) ≤ b.
refined_question: For the class of sets of reals X satisfying S1(Γ, Γ), where Γ(X) is the family of nontrivial open γ-covers of X (that is, infinite open covers U of X such that every x in X belongs to all but finitely many members of U), and S1(Γ, Γ) means that for every sequence ⟨U_n : n in ω⟩ from Γ(X) there exist choices U_n in U_n such that {U_n : n in ω} is again a γ-cover of X, is the additivity number add(S1(Γ, Γ))—the least cardinal κ for which there is a family {X_α : α < κ} of sets of reals each satisfying S1(Γ, Γ) but with ⋃_{α<κ} X_α failing S1(Γ, Γ)—equal to the bounding number b, the least cardinality of an ≤*-unbounded subset of ω^ω?
justification: The draft matches the paper's exact target: Section 8.3, Problem 11 asks precisely whether add(S1(Γ, Γ)) = b (pp. 190-191). To make the question stand-alone while staying faithful to the paper, one must unpack several conventions that the survey leaves implicit at that point: Section 2.3 fixes the default ambient setting to sets of reals (p. 183); Section 2.1 defines the selection principle S1(U, V) (p. 182); Section 3 defines nontrivial covers, γ-covers, and the notation Γ (p. 183); and Section 6 defines b via eventual domination in ω^ω and notes that b is the critical cardinality of S1(Γ, Γ) (p. 186). Since the survey does not restate the meaning of add(P) for a class P at Problem 11, the refined question explicitly spells it out in the standard union/additivity sense suggested by the surrounding discussion in Section 8.3 and by the paper's explicit ideal notation add(I) in Section 7 (pp. 188-189). The paper also records the known bounds h ≤ add(S1(Γ, Γ)) ≤ b in Problem 11 itself, and later notes that this problem is related to Problem 45 via Scheepers' Conjecture 46, which would make the two coincide if true (pp. 203-204).
